set.body:
## Scope
Expose the core local activity reader, active work, attention state, and monitor health through MCP. Complete the CLI-facing compatibility and migration path for existing `watch` and event cursor users.

## Acceptance criteria
- MCP can return bounded recent activity, active work, attention, source freshness/gaps, and monitor health from local state without requiring a live SSH connection.
- MCP, CLI, and library readers agree on activity ordering, attention projection, evidence identity, and cursor semantics for the same journal state.
- Existing watch exit semantics and legacy event cursor behavior remain supported; new readers are not silently substituted for existing consumers.
- Any optional import of legacy terminal events is labeled with its source/limitations and is idempotent.
- Public docs and the remoteslurm skill describe authority boundaries, cursor rules, monitor lifecycle, offline behavior, retention, migration behavior, and the fact that recommendations are not authorization.
- Tests cover local-only MCP read, unavailable remote source, legacy consumer compatibility, and malformed/expired cursor handling.
set.title: A4.1: expose local activity and monitor health through MCP and preserve watch compatibility
